The division rc=aq+s identifies its unique multiset and exact value. The Euclidean squared-distance variance identity and the normal-cone projection condition establish every nonvertex equality case: residuals collide only when \(s=c\), producing precisely the stated coordinate faces. value.rationale: Partition matroids are canonical direct sums and appear naturally as common cells in matroidal hypersimplex multisplits (Schröter 2017). The exact worst Euclidean loss from imposing r identical block quotas is a natural geometric stability invariant for that comparison. The closed formula works for every rank, every quota and every block count, and the nonvertex farthest-locus theorem identifies a sharp number-theoretic transition to many positive-dimensional extremal faces, not merely a one-off or tabulated calculation. It distinguishes when the maximum loss is confined to binary designs and when whole continuum families tie.
